data.narrative: The student implemented a production-grade cache-aside layer using Redis and NestJS. They correctly designed cache eviction hooks on link updates, demonstrated graceful degradation to the primary database when Redis is stopped, and verified latency reductions on cache hits.

dimension_scores.observation: Selected cache-aside over write-through, explicitly reasoning that read-heavy workloads benefit from simple cache-aside patterns while accepting that manual eviction must be implemented on mutations.
dimension_scores.evidence: Cache-aside chosen: GET /r/:code checks Redis first, falls back to MongoDB on miss, sets 300s TTL. LinksService.update evicts key via DEL on PATCH.

dimension_scores.observation: Systematically diagnosed the Redis connection configuration and validated that lazy connect vs eager connect determines connection readiness on startup.
dimension_scores.evidence: Removed lazyConnect and confirmed immediate connection readiness; verified connection error fallback warnings when Redis was stopped.

dimension_scores.observation: Articulated that caching authenticated endpoints or multi-tenant data requires namespace partitioning by tenant and user to prevent cross-account cache leakage.
dimension_scores.evidence: Identified that caching auth data without user-scoped keys leads to privilege escalation and authorization bypass.

dimension_scores.observation: Implemented and tested complete resilience drill: stopped the Redis container and verified that requests did not hang or throw 500s, but seamlessly degraded to MongoDB queries with 302 Found returned.
dimension_scores.evidence: docker stop upsk-redis produced graceful fallback: curl /r/2Sd8OX4z returned HTTP 302 Found, latency 5ms, non-fatal cache warning logged.

dimension_scores.observation: Documented the cache key strategy, TTL selection, and mutation invalidation paths clearly with command evidence.
dimension_scores.evidence: Clearly documented redirect:${code} namespace, 300s TTL, and PATCH invalidation lifecycle.

strengths: Demonstrated resilience by verifying Redis failure fallback directly with Docker container stop and start drills.
Prevented stale data bugs by explicitly coupling database mutations to cache key eviction.
data.recommendation: In Module 07, apply rate limiting and concurrency throttling to protect against cache stampedes on cold starts.

public_evidence.student_action: Implemented Redis cache-aside redirect service with automatic failover to MongoDB and invalidation on PATCH updates.
public_evidence.technical_detail: ioredis integration with 300s TTL, getRedirectTarget, setRedirectTarget, and invalidateRedirectTarget in NestJS.
public_evidence.proof: curl -i http://localhost:3000/r/2Sd8OX4z returned 302 with Cache HIT at 1ms latency; docker stop upsk-redis returned 302 with DB fallback at 5ms latency.
public_evidence.ability: Architects high-performance caching layers with graceful degradation and zero-stale-read guarantees.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows real-world resilience thinking: performance optimization that never compromises system availability or data correctness when cache dependencies fail.

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Checked Redis first, populated on miss with TTL, invalidated on update.
Continued serving HTTP 302 redirects from MongoDB when Redis container was stopped.

teaching_approaches.detail: Proved eviction with update-link PATCH followed by redirect to new destination.

learning_style_signals: Responds effectively to reproducible Docker container stop/start verification commands.
